metadata.note: Command teardown of ./art icon-build (single dispatcher branch at art:64-66; NO aliases in this case). The middle body walks the problem (12 GB / 2.4 M svg files upstream), the four rules that throw work away on purpose (stroke only, one-per-thing, one geometry, B&W), the 44 pt math (24-unit viewBox with stroke 2 renders 44pt at 528px), the --dry-run preview, the --limit trial cut, and the output artifacts (icons/svg/*.svg + icons.json + NOTICE.md carrying the ISC/MIT licence). Falsifiability beat: the four EXCLUDED libraries and why — anthropics has no LICENSE (provenance), RemixIcon is 100% filled (rule 1), material-design-icons is filled AND 9.1 GB (rule 1 + rule 2), heroicons duplicates lucide (rule 2). All demo output in demo/RUN-LOG.md is verbatim from this workspace (svg/ symlinked to public brutalist.art/svg for reproducible dry runs; the shipped canonical set was NOT overwritten). Playlist adaptation for @HumanitariansAI: composer folder chip reads @HumanitariansAI; outro card is the locked ClaudeTitleOutro with hardcoded @NikBearBrown handle per OUTRO-LOCK.md — flagged for the human reviewer before publication. No paid API, no upload, no re-cut of the shipped set. episode.source_sha256 50810aad5f8e2dfbf0928ecee7a233beca952f35d6220a9706eb3847aa5c5a38.

beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — Claude UI cold open. Ask lands answered; narration introduces Liam in for Bear.
beats.narration_text: Merhaba, this is Liam, in for Bear. There are twelve gigabytes of raw icons in the svg folder. Two point four million files. Nobody ships that. Art icon-build cuts a set you can actually put in git. Thirty megabytes. Seven thousand three hundred icons. One geometry, one line width, one color hook.

beats.role_note: EXECUTIVE-SUMMARY LAW — Beat 2 BLUF, written by the hesitant writer. Corrects the reel's actual misconception.
beats.narration_text: Watch the writer walk this back. Art icon-build does not download new icons. It cuts a canonical set from ones that already sit on disk. Twelve gigabytes in, thirty megabytes out. Subtractive, not additive — and that is the difference this whole reel turns on.

show.event: first lines type: 'art icon-build downloads / new icons.'

beats.role_note: FRAMEWORK — the dispatcher. One case branch, no aliases, one exec.
beats.narration_text: The dispatcher is one case branch in the art file. No aliases this time — only the exact word icon-build hits it. That branch execs a single python script, build_icon_set dot py. Everything else in this film is what that script actually does.

show.event: code card fades in with 'art' in the title bar
spark line settles under the card

props.title: art:64-66 — one branch, no aliases
props.code:
# From the top-level art dispatcher:
case "$cmd" in
  # …
  icon-build)
    exec python3 "$ART_HOME/runtime/scripts/build_icon_set.py" "$@"
    ;;
  # …
esac

# For contrast, the neighbouring branch takes THREE aliases:
#   icons|icon|icon-search)   →   icon_search.py
# icon-build stands alone. Rarely needed, one word only.
props.sparkLine: One word. One branch. One script.

beats.role_note: MECHANISM — THE PROBLEM. 12 GB / 2.4 M files. Almost all variants. Not shippable, not searchable.
beats.narration_text: The problem it solves. The svg folder holds a dozen upstream icon libraries. Twelve gigabytes on disk. Two point four million files. Almost all of it is variants — every style, every density, every platform — of a much smaller number of actual ideas. None of it fits in git. None of it is searchable. That is the corpus icon-build turns into something you can ship.

show.event: card in; title reads 'svg/ — the raw upstream libraries'

  30 M   svg/iconoir           (stroke, MIT)
  18 M   svg/feather           (stroke, MIT)

  9.1 GB svg/material-design-icons   (filled — 1.79 M files)
  59 M   svg/RemixIcon                (100% filled)
  14 M   svg/heroicons                (mostly solid)
  3.1 M  svg/anthropics               (stroke, NO LICENSE)

  12 GB  svg/    (total on disk, ~2.4 M files)

# None of this is shippable, none of it is searchable.
# icon-build is the cut that produces something that IS.
props.sparkLine: 12 GB in. Almost all variants of the same ideas.

beats.role_note: MECHANISM — THE FOUR RULES. Each throws work away on purpose.
beats.narration_text: Four rules do the cutting. Rule one: stroke only. A filled icon has no line width, so filled libraries are dropped whole. Rule two: one icon per thing. Names are normalised — the same concept in five outline styles collapses to one. Rule three: one geometry, one weight. Everything is rewritten to a twenty-four unit viewBox and stroke width two. Rule four: black and white. Every color becomes currentColor, so one icon serves ink on cream and cream on ink.

show.event: card in; title reads 'THE FOUR RULES (each one throws work away on purpose)'

props.title: build_icon_set.py:14-27 — the four rules
props.code:
# From the module docstring:

#   1. STROKE ONLY.  A filled icon has no line width, so filled
#      libraries are dropped whole.

#   2. ONE ICON PER THING.  Names are normalised (case, separators,
#      the -outline / -filled / -16 / -24 suffix noise) and the FIRST
#      library in PRIORITY order to claim a concept keeps it.

#   3. ONE GEOMETRY, ONE WEIGHT.  Everything is rewritten to
#      viewBox 0 0 24 24, fill='none', stroke='currentColor',
#      stroke-width=2, round caps/joins.

#   4. B&W.  Any hard-coded colour becomes currentColor, so ONE icon
#      serves ink on cream AND cream on ink without a second file.
props.sparkLine: One weight. One geometry. One color hook.

beats.role_note: MECHANISM — THE 44pt MATH. Why stroke 2 in a 24 viewBox is the '44pt' set.
beats.narration_text: Here is why twenty-four and two is the forty-four point set. A stroke of two in a twenty-four unit viewBox scales with the render. At the canonical render size, five hundred and twenty-eight pixels, two times five twenty-eight over twenty-four is forty-four, exactly. That constant ships in icons dot json as line-forty-four-pt-px, so a beat never has to rediscover it. Render smaller and the line stays proportional. That is the point of normalising the source instead of baking a pixel width in.

show.event: card in; title reads 'the 44 pt math — stroke 2 in a 24 viewBox'

props.title: build_icon_set.py:53-56 — the 44 pt math
props.code:
VIEWBOX             = "0 0 24 24"
STROKE_W            = 2
RENDER_PX_FOR_44PT  = 528     # 2 * (528 / 24) == 44

#             stroke        render          line weight
#     ----------------  x  --------  =  ------------------
#     viewBox width         (px)              (pt)
#
#             2 / 24     x    528     =    44 pt   ✓

# Ships in the index so beats never rediscover it:
"render": {
  "line_44pt_px": 528,
  "note": "stroke 2 in a 24 viewBox = 44pt at 528px;
           scales proportionally"
}

beats.role_note: WORKED EXAMPLE — verbatim --dry-run output from this workspace.
beats.narration_text: Dot slash art icon-build dash dash dry-run. Every run reports the source passes in priority order. Lucide keeps seventeen forty-nine, drops seven duplicates. Tabler keeps four thousand one thirty-four, drops six hundred and two. Iconoir keeps ten forty-five, drops six hundred and twenty-six. Feather keeps only twenty-six because lucide already owns the others. Brand keeps three hundred and seventy-six. Total: seven thousand three hundred and thirty. Nothing written to disk.

beats.role_note: WORKED EXAMPLE — the output artifacts. icons/svg + icons.json + NOTICE.md carries the licences.
beats.narration_text: Drop the dash dash dry-run and it writes three things. A folder of seven thousand three hundred and thirty svg files, one per concept. An index file, icons dot json, that names each one, its source pack, its tokens, and whether it is a logo. And a NOTICE dot md that carries the ISC and MIT copyright notices, in full. That last one is the licence obligation, met.

show.event: card in; title reads 'output artifacts (~30 MB, shippable in git)'

props.title: $ ls icons/  &&  head icons/NOTICE.md
props.code:
icons/
├── svg/           # 7,330 .svg files — one per concept, 29 MB
│   ├── database.svg
│   ├── brand-github.svg
│   └── …
├── icons.json     # the index (count, geometry, tokens, sources)
└── NOTICE.md      # ISC (lucide) + MIT (tabler, iconoir, feather)

# icons.json — the manifest
{ "canonical": true, "count": 7330,
  "geometry": {"viewBox":"0 0 24 24","stroke_width":2,
               "stroke":"currentColor","fill":"none"},
  "sources": {"lucide": "kept 1749…", "tabler": "kept 4134…", …} }

# NOTICE.md — the licence obligation, MET
# These icons are MODIFIED copies: every icon rewritten to a single
# geometry, single line width, currentColor. ISC and MIT both permit
# that, on the condition that the copyright notice travels with the
# work. It is reproduced in full below.
props.sparkLine: svg/ · icons.json · NOTICE.md — one shippable set.

beats.role_note: FALSIFIABILITY — the principled exclusions. Four upstream libraries dropped, each for a reason.
beats.narration_text: And here is what the tool refuses to include. Material design icons: filled, and nine point one gigabytes on its own — rule one and rule two. Remix icon: one hundred percent filled — rule one. Heroicons: its outline set duplicates lucide, which lucide already serves at a cleaner single weight — rule two. Anthropics: no LICENSE file anywhere. Unknown provenance cannot be redistributed. Every drop is named in the module docstring. Nothing is silently swept in.

show.event: card in; title reads 'EXCLUDED ON PURPOSE (build_icon_set.py:68-76)'
four rows type in one at a time with the reason next to each
doctrine line lands: 'do not re-add without resolving the reason'

props.title: # EXCLUDED ON PURPOSE — do not re-add without resolving the reason
props.code:
material-design-icons/  filled, 1.79 M files / 9.1 GB
                        →  rule 1 (stroke only)  +  rule 2 (one per thing)

RemixIcon/              100% filled
                        →  rule 1 (no line width to normalise)

heroicons/              mostly solid; its outline set duplicates lucide
                        →  rule 2 (first-in-priority keeps the concept)

anthropics/             614 stroke icons, NO LICENSE FILE
                        →  unknown provenance cannot be redistributed
                           (resolve the source and its licence FIRST)

# The doctrine: every drop is named, with the reason. Nothing is
# silently swept in. Re-adding one is a licence question, not a
# preference change.
props.sparkLine: Every drop is named. Nothing swept in silently.

beats.role_note: VERDICT — the whole surface. Four moves, plus the discipline the four rules encode.
beats.narration_text: So the surface. Bare art icon-build re-cuts the whole set and writes it to icons slash. Dash dash dry-run reports the same passes without writing. Dash dash limit N takes a small trial. Under the hood, four rules throw work away on purpose, one dispatcher branch runs the whole thing, and one NOTICE dot md carries the ISC and MIT copyright notices out with every ship. Twelve gigabytes of raw variants become thirty megabytes of shippable line drawings.

props.artifactHeading: art icon-build — the whole surface, in the order you actually use it
artifactLines: bare invocation — re-cuts icons/ from svg/; writes ~30 MB (svg/, icons.json, NOTICE.md).
--dry-run — reports the same source passes without writing; safe to run any time.
--limit N — small trial cut; stops at the first N icons from the first source.
the four rules — stroke only · one-icon-per-thing · one geometry/weight · B&W.
the four exclusions — material-design (filled), RemixIcon (filled), heroicons (dup), anthropics (no LICENSE).
the 44 pt math — stroke 2 in a 24 viewBox at 528 px = 44 pt exactly; ships in icons.json.
NOTICE.md — the licence obligation, met: ISC + MIT travel with every shipped set.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — Your Turn composer. Prompt read aloud verbatim, then discussed.
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude Code from the brutalist toolkit root. It runs the safe preview, a limited trial, and then reads three things off the shipped set: the count, the geometry, and the first two ISC-and-MIT license names in NOTICE dot md. What you want to see: same seven thousand three hundred and thirty in the preview and in the JSON, the trial cut stops at your limit, and NOTICE contains both an ISC block and an MIT block. If the preview count drifts from the JSON count, that is a lead — svg has changed since the last cut and the shipped set is stale.

props.segment: Audit art icon-build on the shipped set
props.command: From the brutalist.art toolkit root: (1) ./art icon-build --dry-run  and note the CANONICAL SET count. (2) ./art icon-build --limit 3 --dry-run  and confirm it stops at 3 in the first source only. (3) python3 -c 'import json; d=json.load(open("icons/icons.json")); print(d["count"], sum(1 for i in d["icons"] if i["brand"]))'  and compare to (1). (4) grep -c '^## ' icons/NOTICE.md  and open the file: at least an ISC block (lucide) and an MIT block (tabler / iconoir / feather) must be present.
output: (1) dry-run reports 7,330 concepts (376 brand/logo) — priority order preserved
(2) --limit 3 --dry-run stops in lucide only; other sources not touched
(3) icons.json count == dry-run count (drift means the set is stale)
(4) NOTICE.md contains an ISC block AND an MIT block, verbatim from upstream
